archetype.name: Bubble Team (goaltending-first)
archetype.definition: A club whose results rest on an elite goalie and a stingy goals-against line while it gets out-chanced at 5-on-5. That keeps it in the Metropolitan playoff conversation without making it a team that controls games.

report.headline: Sorokin is propping up a .500 start the underlying play hasn't earned
report.take:
Six games in, the Islanders look the way they have looked for years. They allow few goals, hang around in every game, and lean hard on the man in net. Ilya Sorokin has started five of the six with a .934 save percentage and 5.6 goals saved above expected, which is the whole team's GSAx and ranks 4th in the league. History says this isn't new. The 2022-23 and 2025-26 teams both finished 5th in Def Rank with team GSAx above 40, and both did it while posting offenses in the bottom third. This roster's identity is goaltending, and it shows again.

The odd part is the record. A Goal Diff / GP of 0.67, 10th in the league, usually comes with more than 3-3-0. The Pts vs Goal Diff of -2 ranks 31st: every loss has come in regulation, and the wins and losses have alternated without a streak longer than one. That margin is a little flattering, though. A huge share of it came from a single night, the 6-0 home win over New Jersey. The rest of the schedule has looked much closer to even.

The numbers hide how much of the start is Sorokin and hot finishing rather than control of play. At 5-on-5 the Islanders own 48.9% of expected goals (22nd) and 48% of shot attempts (19th). A PDO of 104.3 is the kind of figure that drifts back toward 100. The offense has been better than usual: 15th in Off Rank against a recent run of 22nd-to-28th finishes, and the power play at 21.1% after last year's 16.5%. Bo Horvat drives much of it, with 7 points, 4 of them on the power play. Rookie-level minutes for Matthew Schaefer, at 25.42 a night, tell you the blueline behind him is thin, and the C- grade backs that up.

The likely path from here is a team that keeps winning low-event games when Sorokin is on and struggles to stop the slide when he isn't. The close-game bad luck should even out and give back some points. The shooting and save-percentage boost should cool and take some away. Both corrections land near where this franchise usually sits: somewhere around the playoff line.

strengths.title: Sorokin is stealing goals again
strengths.body: Sorokin ranks 3rd of 64 on the goalie tab with a 1.81 GAA and a shutout. His 5.6 GSAx is what turns a below-average 5-on-5 team into a top-ten defense by goals against. The pace will cool, but this franchise has posted team GSAx above 40 twice in the last four seasons. Elite goaltending here is a durable trait, not a fluke.

strengths.title: Horvat and a functional power play
strengths.body: Horvat leads the forwards in points and shots, and he sits 14th of 213 on the center tab with a 53.3% xGF share. The power play is converting at a league-middle 21.1%. That is a real step up from last season's 16.5% and the 12.6% of the year before. A mid-pack power play is worth a lot to a team that can't create much at even strength, though six games is a thin sample to bank on.

strengths.title: Centers kept quiet
strengths.body: Opposing centers are producing under their usual output against this group (rank 5). Centers' share of the points allowed is well below the league norm. Forwards overall are held 1.4 points a game under expectation. Much of that comes from Sorokin turning away chances rather than from the skaters suppressing them.

concerns.title: Getting out-chanced at 5-on-5
concerns.body: An xGF % of 48.9% and a CF % of 48% put the Islanders in the bottom half of the league at controlling play. The PDO of 104.3 says finishing and saves are covering the gap. That pattern has followed this team for years. When the percentages normalize, the goal differential will shrink unless the chance share improves.

concerns.title: A blueline leaning on one player
concerns.body: The defense grades C- even with Schaefer playing over 25 minutes a night and sitting 24th of 239 on his tab. Ryan Pulock is 220th, with no points and a 42.1% xGF share in more than 18 minutes. Opposing defensemen are out-producing their norms against this team (rank 22), and the defense gives up a larger-than-normal share of its points to the back end. The group grade is Schaefer plus a lot of soft minutes.

concerns.title: Record behind the margin, for now
concerns.body: A Pts vs Goal Diff of -2, 31st in the league, means the Islanders have banked fewer points than their goals for and against suggest. Every loss has come in regulation. That tends to even out. But the margin it is measured against is inflated by one 6-0 rout, so the correction may be smaller than it looks.

trend.note: Win, loss, win, loss: the Islanders haven't strung together two of either. The 6-0 win over New Jersey and the 5-2 and 5-3 losses to the Rangers and Tampa Bay show how much nightly results swing with the goaltending and finishing.

weekAhead.headline: Two road tests, then home dates with Anaheim and Los Angeles
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with a back-to-back-style road swing to Ottawa and Toronto. Neither team out-chances opponents: Ottawa's 44% CF % ranks 27th and Toronto's 41.1% xGF % ranks 28th. These should be low-margin games where Sorokin matters most. Ottawa is also riding close-game luck, with Pts vs Goal Diff 3rd in the league, so its 5-2-0 overstates it. Toronto already beat the Islanders 2-1 on opening night.

Back home, Anaheim is the toughest opponent on paper, 9th on the site with a power play converting a third of its chances. Los Angeles sits 31st, but the Kings are better than 0-3-2: their shot share ranks 10th and their PDO of 93.5 is historically unlucky. Their goaltending and penalty kill are what's broken. A split on the road and a sweep at home is a reasonable target.

keyMatchups.title: Islanders power play vs Kings' kill
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles is killing only 57.9% of penalties, 31st in the league. Its goalies are 8.1 goals below expected. For an offense that has historically struggled to score, the Kings game is the best chance all week to get Horvat and Schaefer's power-play unit rolling.

keyMatchups.title: Discipline against Toronto and Anaheim
keyMatchups.body: Toronto's power play converts 29.2% (5th) and Anaheim's 33.3% (3rd). The Islanders' kill is middle-of-the-pack at 82.6%. Meanwhile Toronto's PK has allowed almost nothing at 95.8%, so trading penalties with the Leafs is a losing deal.

keyMatchups.title: Islander wingers against soft coverage
keyMatchups.body: Ottawa allows wingers 0.78 points a game over expectation (rank 25), and Los Angeles 1.15 over (rank 29). Maccelli, with 5 points and a 57% xGF share, and Heineman, at 55%, are the wingers best placed to cash in.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the Islanders can win the shot battle against Ottawa and Toronto, two teams that also get out-attempted. If not, the week rides entirely on Sorokin.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the Islanders to settle into their familiar band: a top-ten goals-against team built on Sorokin, a middling-to-weak offense, and a record within a few points of the Metropolitan cut line. The close-game bad luck should flip somewhat in their favor. The 104.3 PDO and Sorokin's .934 should drift down, so the goal differential should narrow even as the points catch up to it.

The sustainable pieces are the goaltending and, possibly, a power play that is finally average. The fragile ones are the shooting luck and a blueline that depends on Schaefer's heavy minutes. If the 5-on-5 share stays below 49%, this is a bubble team. If Horvat's line and the power play keep the offense near the league middle, it can be a playoff team.
swingFactors: Whether the power play holds above 20%
Depth on the blueline behind Schaefer

confidence.note: Six games; PDO and goalie numbers are far from settled.
